idiom_name: DAO interface + constructor function per store over a database/sql handle
implementation_notes: Go's implicit interfaces make the DAO interface and its implementations ordinary: declare type UserDAO interface { ... }, implement one struct per store, and replace the factory class with a constructor function or a small switch on the configured driver - there is no hierarchy to build. The store-selection half is already in the standard library: sql.Open(driverName, dsn) resolves a driver registered via sql.Register in the driver's init() and returns a store-agnostic *sql.DB pool, so the DAO constructor receives the same handle whatever the backend. A hand-written factory type is justified only when DAO construction needs per-store arguments a DSN cannot carry.
pitfalls: database/sql pools per *sql.DB and never closes connections on its own: one DB per store or tenant must be created (and closed) at the composition root, and SetMaxOpenConns should be set before load.
Driver packages register themselves through a blank import (import _ "github.com/lib/pq"); a missing import fails at sql.Open with sql: unknown driver, which is easy to misread as a DSN problem.
A store-name switch repeated in every constructor drifts; beyond a couple of stores keep one registry (map[string]func(*sql.DB) (UserDAO, error)) keyed by driver name.
